Alternate art is where the money is

The One Piece Card Game prices its alternate art printings far above the standard versions of the same card, and manga-art treatments higher again. The card number can be identical while the artwork differs.

That makes art variant a field to confirm, not something to infer from the card name. Card AI suggests catalog matches; you review the artwork and select the correct record before pricing it.

Leader cards and parallels tracked as their own entries

Leaders, parallels and the standard run of a card each trade separately. Recording them as one line item hides what your collection is actually worth.

Card AI stores the set, card number, variant and finish per card, so every printing you own sits in the collection as a distinct position with its own price.

Japanese and English copies are separate markets

One Piece runs parallel Japanese and English releases, and the same card frequently trades at different prices in each. Language is part of every card record, so the two are tracked and valued independently rather than blended.

One Piece card scanner questions.

Can Card AI tell alternate art from the standard printing?

The scan suggests likely records, but alternate art can share a card number with the standard version. Review the artwork and confirm the correct record before adding or pricing it.

Does it work on Japanese One Piece cards?

Language is tracked per card, so Japanese and English copies are stored as separate entries with their own market prices.

Can I track One Piece alongside other games?

Yes. One Piece and other supported games can share a collection with a single running total.

Can I check One Piece card prices without the card in hand?

Yes. The One Piece card price checker works from search as well as from a scan, so you can look up one piece card value before buying. Cards you own become a one piece card collection tracker with a live total.
